```{r}
library(ggplot2)
data("trees")
head(trees)
```
#Q1
```{r}
hist(trees$Girth,
     main="Distribution of Girth in Trees",
     xlab = "Girth",
     col="pink")

```

#Q2
```{r}
hist(trees$Volume,
     main="Distribution of Volume in trees",
     xlab = "Volume",
     col="purple")

```


#Q3
```{r}
plot(
  trees$Girth~trees$Volume,
  type="p",
  lwd=2,
  col="green",
  xlab="Tree Volume",
  ylab="Tree Girth",
  main="Relationship between Tree Volume and Girth",
)
```

#Q4
```{r}
shapiro.test(trees$Volume)
#p-value= 0.003229, this indicates that Volume does not have a normal distribution.

```

#Q5
```{r}
shapiro.test(trees$Girth)
#p value=0.08893, this indicates a normal distribution because the value is >0.05
```
